## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical equipment problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running without hydraulic load, indicating either a dry-run condition, impeller failure, or discharge line disconnection. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating. All other components inspected during this visit were in good condition and operating normally.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The tank liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter was in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% FLA | CRITICAL |

The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage. This indicates the pump is operating without adequate hydraulic load. The motor is at risk of overheating because it is not being cooled by fluid circulation. The most likely causes are: the pump is running dry (no fluid in the discharge line or tank level has dropped below the pump intake), the impeller is broken or missing, or the discharge line is severed or disconnected downstream of the pump.

The high water alarm tested functional and electrical connections are sound.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE PRIORITY:**
- **Immediate professional attention required.** The effluent pump is operating without hydraulic load (22.2% FLA). Do not continue operating the system. A qualified service technician must inspect the pump intake, discharge line, and impeller to determine whether the pump is running dry, the impeller is damaged, or the discharge line is blocked or disconnected. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**SECONDARY:**
- Once the pump load condition is resolved, continue the current 12-month maintenance interval.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

Your system has a pump problem that needs immediate attention. The pump is running but not moving water, which will damage the motor if it continues. This can happen if the tank level drops too low, if the discharge pipe is blocked or broken, or if the pump's internal parts have failed. Do not use the system until a technician has checked and repaired the pump. Call for service today.
